newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Jewish report to slam bomb probes.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Jewish report to slam bomb probes.

text.p: Argentine Jewish community leader Ruben Beraja said on Wednesday he will present authorities with a report next week criticising investigations into two bombings which killed 115 people.

Argentine Jews are increasingly angry over the lack of progress of investigations into the bombing of their Buenos Aires community centre, which killed 86 people in 1994, and of the Israeli embassy, which killed 29 people two years earlier.
Beraja said he will hand the report to Judge Juan Jose Galeano, who is in charge of the investigation into the car-bombing of the AMIA community centre.
"This is an ordered list of the judicial, police and administrative actions which have caused omissions, deficiencies, and complications in the investigation," Beraja told a news conference.
"In each case the person responsible is identified," he said, explaining that the purpose of the report is to help Galeano hone his investigation.
Beraja said media stories describing the document as a list of officials obstructing the probes were regrettable, and added that no top government officials are named.
Beraja has himself come under fire from Jews who think he has not pressured the government enough over the bombings.

He got an angry reception last Friday from sections of a crowd which gathered to commemorate the third anniversary of the AMIA attack. Protestors interrupted his speech by shouting at him to name the officials implicated in his report.

Israel has also voiced its displeasure at the investigations. Ambassador Yitzhak Aviran met President Carlos Menem on Monday to discuss the bombings, which Israel believes were carried out by Iranian-backed guerrillas.

No one is under arrest for the embassy bombing. In the AMIA probe, three policeman and a car thief have been charged with providing the vehicle used, and Iran has been named as the instigator, but the bombers are still at large.
